import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('/data/worldbank_education_gdp.csv')

# Define the relevant series names
relevant_series_names = [
    'Labor force participation rate, total (percentage of total population ages 15+) (modeled ILO estimate)',
    'School enrollment, primary (percentage gross)',
    'School enrollment, secondary (percentage gross)',
    'Exports of goods and services (annual percentage growth)'
]

# Filter the dataset to include only the relevant series names
df_relevant = df[df['Series Name'].isin(relevant_series_names)]

# Extract the year columns
year_columns = [col for col in df.columns if col.startswith('19') or col.startswith('20')]

# Create a new DataFrame with only the relevant series names and year columns
df_years = df_relevant[['Country Group', 'Country Code', 'Series Name'] + year_columns]

# Melt the DataFrame to have one row per country, year, and series name
df_melted = df_years.melt(id_vars=['Country Group', 'Country Code', 'Series Name'], var_name='Year', value_name='Value')

# Convert the 'Value' column to numeric, handling any non-numeric values
df_melted['Value'] = pd.to_numeric(df_melted['Value'], errors='coerce')

# Drop rows with missing values in the relevant columns
df_clean = df_melted.dropna(subset=['Value', 'Series Name', 'Year'])

# Extract the numeric year from the 'Year' column
df_clean['Year'] = df_clean['Year'].str.extract(r'(\d{4})', expand=False).astype(int)

# Group the data by 'Country Code' and 'Year' to ensure one row per country and year
df_grouped = df_clean.groupby(['Country Code', 'Year', 'Series Name'])['Value'].mean().reset_index()

# Pivot the data to have one row per country and year with columns for each series
df_pivot = df_grouped.pivot_table(index=['Country Code', 'Year'], columns='Series Name', values='Value').reset_index()

# Calculate the correlation matrix
correlation_matrix = df_pivot.corr()

# Display the correlation matrix
correlation_matrix
